core.text: Keep the objective fixed: eight registrations and eight distinct recognized receipts by boundary 9 within six dispatcher actions. Exact comparison metric is distinct recognitions by boundary 9; both doses complete eight registrations.

Predeclare registration order N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Normal dose: individual N2 at 0, N3 at 1, N4 at 2, bulk at 4, individual N7 at 5 and N8 at 6. Higher dose: replace only the tick-0 individual with bulk; retain all other actions. Both spend six actions; bulk dose increases from one to two. Finite-model predictions are normal eight recognitions, higher seven. These are deductions, not measured benefits.

Fixed trigger: compare the declared doses in two independently reset matched trial pairs with identical initial demand, timings and states. Switch only if each higher-dose trial has fewer distinct recognitions than its normal-dose control; otherwise hold. Inspect registrations, distinct recognitions, queue duplicates and action totals. Reset and four-trial resources are not supplied; trial execution is an untestable assumption, not an authorized observation.

No opening: the available dependency-free route would deprive the bulk tool and use individual requests only. Seven remaining identities need seven individual actions, exceeding six available. Its recognition ceiling is seven including N1, so it cannot preserve the fixed success function. Do not activate this exit even if the harmful-dose trigger were confirmed. Concrete feasible action is the normal schedule; closest rival is the declared higher-dose schedule.

residue.text: N1 recognition survives its pending display. Higher dose inserts its duplicate at tick 1, shifting N4 recognition to tick 4; the tick-4 bulk then queues another N4 receipt. That duplicate consumes tick 5 and leaves N8 beyond the window. Preserve these queue facts rather than equating pending status with unmet recognition.

Actor burden: six one-tick validations and six dispatcher actions per modeled schedule; ledgers add no clerk labor. Defeat would be a conforming replay contradicting the predicted counts or evidence of a feasible bulk-free route achieving eight under these constraints. Display-delay origin, later sender adaptation and empirical generalization remain unknown. No observed threshold, successful execution or global-optimality proof is claimed.

tension.account_a: Increasing bulk use can consume scarce delivery slots through stale-pending duplicates and worsen the present goal.
tension.account_b: Increasing bulk use provides additional useful coverage sufficient to retain all eight recognitions.
tension.prediction_a: For the fixed pair, each reset replay yields eight normal-dose recognitions versus seven higher-dose recognitions by boundary 9.
tension.prediction_b: For that same pair, the higher dose still yields eight recognitions; the modeled seventh-only result defeats this account.
